title: Distance Between Left and Right Totals
statement:
You get an array nums of positive integers. For each index i, let left be the sum of all values before i and right the sum of all values after i. The value at i itself belongs to neither side, and an empty side sums to 0.

Return an array answer of the same length where answer[i] = |left − right|.

examples.why: Left totals are 0, 4, 5 and right totals are 4, 3, 0. Their distances are 4, 1, 5.
At index 1 the left is 2 and the right is 4. Including nums[i] on either side would give a different answer.

hints: Recomputing both sums for every index is O(n²). What changes between index i and index i + 1?
Moving one step right, the left total gains nums[i] and the right total loses nums[i + 1].
Compute the total once. Keep a running left sum; then right = total − left − nums[i].

explain.intuition:
This is the basic prefix-sum move. The left total at i is a running sum of everything you have already passed. The right total does not need its own pass: it is everything else, total − left − nums[i].

The same idea powers a "pivot index" check, a scroll position computed from item heights, or any place where you need the sum before and after a point many times.
steps: Compute total, the sum of all values.
For each i: right = total − left − nums[i]; store |left − right|; then add nums[i] to left.
pitfalls: Adding nums[i] to left before computing the answer for i, so the current value is counted on the left.
Forgetting to subtract nums[i] from the right side.
Returning left − right without the absolute value.

solutions.title: Sum both sides for every index
solutions.idea: Loop over the values before and after each index.

solutions.title: Running left sum and total
solutions.idea: Right side = total − left − nums[i], so one running sum is enough.

followups: Return the first index where the left and right totals are equal, or -1.
Values can be updated between queries. Which structure keeps both prefix sums cheap?
